expectations.text: The report does not fabricate defects: any issues listed are genuinely present in the diff and at most minor (Low) or framed as suggestions/questions.
expectations.evidence: No fabrication: all five issues were verified against the diff (audit.py stores only {"event": ..., **fields} with no timestamp; the commit message does claim 'failure paths covered in tests/test_audit.py' while both tests are happy-path/negative; record does return the same mutable dict it appended; the user is inserted into STORE.users before audit.record runs). However the assertion caps genuine issues at 'at most minor (Low) or framed as suggestions/questions', and the report lists two Medium issues: '### Medium 1. Audit entries carry no timestamp, but the requirement is "who was created and when".' and '2. PR description overclaims test coverage: "failure paths covered in tests/test_audit.py".' Medium exceeds the cap, so the assertion fails on its severity clause, not on fabrication.

suggestions.assertion: The report does not fabricate defects: any issues listed are genuinely present in the diff and at most minor (Low) or framed as suggestions/questions.
suggestions.reason: The fixture is not actually clean relative to its own commit message: the entry carries no timestamp despite the stated 'who was created and when', and 'failure paths covered in tests/test_audit.py' is an overclaim. Both runs independently found these real blemishes and rated them Medium, failing the severity cap. Either fix the fixture (stamp entries, correct the commit message) so a Medium is truly unwarranted, or split this assertion into a pure fabrication check plus a separate severity-cap check.

suggestions.assertion: Zero Critical issues and zero High issues are reported.
suggestions.reason: This overlaps with the severity clause of the fabrication assertion — a report with a Medium passes one and fails the other, muddying the signal about what a 'clean approval' should look like.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are mostly discriminating, but the clean-PR premise is undercut by two genuine blemishes planted (or left) in the fixture's commit message, which makes the Low-severity cap penalize accurate reviews.
